title: Anytime-valid confidence sequence for a bounded mean
purpose: Give confidence intervals for the mean of bounded observations that hold at every time simultaneously, so results can be monitored after each run and stopped at any point. Includes a Hoeffding union-bound sequence, a betting (hedged capital) sequence and a seeded coverage simulation.

entry_points.name: hoeffding_sequence
entry_points.arguments: observations in [lower_bound, upper_bound]; alpha in (0, 1); lower_bound; upper_bound
entry_points.returns: {lower, upper, means, final, empty_at, method} as running intersections

entry_points.name: betting_sequence
entry_points.arguments: observations; alpha; lower_bound; upper_bound; grid (20 to 2000 cells); cap in (0, 1)

entry_points.name: pointwise_wilson_sequence
entry_points.returns: the fixed-sample Wilson interval at each t, for comparison

entry_points.name: coverage_simulation
entry_points.arguments: method: hoeffding, betting or pointwise_wilson; mean; length; replications; alpha; seed; grid

assumptions: Observations lie in the stated bounds and share one conditional mean given the past (for example independent and identically distributed).
The level alpha is fixed before looking at the data.
guarantees: hoeffding: P(mu leaves the interval at some t) <= alpha, by Hoeffding's inequality at level alpha / (t (t + 1)) and a union bound.

betting: the averaged capital (K+ + K-) / 2 at the true mean is a non-negative martingale, so P(it ever reaches 1 / alpha) <= alpha by Ville's inequality; the reported intervals contain every candidate mean the capital never rejects.
Running intersections keep the simultaneous guarantee; empty_at records a time when the intersection would have become empty.

known_wrong.name: peeking_is_not_anytime_valid
known_wrong.why: A fixed-sample 90 percent interval checked after every observation misses the mean at some time in about 66 percent of these runs.

limits: Means of bounded observations only; the bounds must be known in advance. The Hoeffding sequence is conservative; the betting sequence is tighter but costs grid x n operations and is meant for up to a few thousand observations. Grid reporting rounds intervals outward by at most one cell. Guarantees need a constant conditional mean; under drift the sequence covers no single target.
technique_references: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting (Waudby-Smith and Ramdas)
Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences (Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe and Sekhon)
Hoeffding's inequality with a union bound over time
